Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:10:1.hebrew: פקע ליה שעבודיה - וקם ליה ברשותי' דמריה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:10:1.english: His lien is abrogated - And [it] stands in the possession of its owner.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:14:1.english: And the halakha - [this refers to] that which we said, "this one acquired the rest."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:14:2.hebrew: בדליתיה - למשכון בחצירו של מלוה בשעת מיתת הגר, אבל איתיה למשכון בחצירו, קני ליה חצירו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:14:2.english: Where it is not - [that is, where] the collateral [is not] in the creditor's courtyard at the time of the convert's death; but [if] the collateral is in his courtyard, his courtyard acquires [it] for him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:15:1.hebrew: ופתחו לרה"ר - וכ"ש אם חפר ברה"ר ופתחו לרשות הרבים, ולא תימא דוקא חופר ברשותיה, דהוה ליה בור דאית ליה בעלים, אבל חפר ברה"ר פטור; דהא תני סיפא: החופר בור ברה"ר ונפל לתוכו כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:15:1.english: And opens it to the public domain - And all the more so if he dug [it] in the public domain and opened it to the public domain. And do not say [that he is liable] specifically [when] digging in his own property, where it is a pit that has an owner, whereas if he dug in the public domain he is exempt — for the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teaches: "One who digs a pit in the public domain and [one] fell into it, etc."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:15:2.hebrew: ברה"ר ופתחו לרה"י - דהוה ליה בור ברה"י, והפקיר רשותו, דלא מצי למימר "מאי בעית ברשותי?", ונפל דרך פיו לתוכו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:15:2.english: In the public domain and opens its [entrance] onto private property - For it is a pit on private property, and he declared his property ownerless, so that he cannot say, "What were you doing on my property?" and [the victim] fell through its opening into it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:15:3.hebrew: חייב - דקסבר חיובא דבור בין ברשות הרבים בין ברשות היחיד היא, ובלבד שיפקיר רשותו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:15:3.english: [He is] liable - For [the Tanna] holds [that] the liability of a pit is [applicable] whether in the public domain [or] in a private domain, provided that he declares his domain ownerless.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:16:1.hebrew: ופתחו לרשות הרבים - כיון שהתקלה ברשות הרבים, הוה ליה כמי שחפרו ברה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:16:1.english: And opens it to the public domain - Since the hazard is in the public domain, it is [considered] as if he dug it in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:16:2.english: And this is Pit, etc. - Later [the Gemara] explains what 'this is' [means].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:17:1.english: Setam - We do not read [this word in the text].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:17:2.hebrew: כ"ע לא פליגי דמיחייב - ור"ע מודה ליה לרבי ישמעאל בבור ברשות הרבים, דהוא אמור בתורה, אבל רבי ישמעאל לא מודי ליה לרבי עקיבא בבור ברשותו, דקסבר: כי אפקרנא לך רשותי, לאו לאחיובי אנא בהזיקא אפקרתיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:17:2.english: Everyone agrees that he is liable - And Rabbi Akiva concedes to Rabbi Yishmael regarding a pit in the public domain, as it is stated in the Torah; however, Rabbi Yishmael does not concede to Rabbi Akiva regarding a pit in his [own] domain, for he holds: "When I declared my domain ownerless for you, I did not declare it ownerless in order for me to become liable for damage."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:17:3.hebrew: אם על פותח - שחפרו אחר וכסהו, ובא אחר וגילהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:17:3.english: If for [one who] opens - Where another [person] dug it and covered it, and another came and uncovered it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:17:4.hebrew: באה לו - שאין לו חלק בו אלא שכרהו או שפתחו, דהיינו ברשות הרבים, שאין הקרקע שלו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:17:4.english: Comes to him - [Meaning] that he has no share in it except that he dug it or opened it — that is, in the public domain, where the land is not his.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:2:1.hebrew: לרבה ודאי - ע"כ מוקי למילתיה כתנאי, דהוא אמר חייב, והא דתני פטור לא מצי מוקי ליה כוותיה; וע"כ הכי מתרץ: אנא דאמרי כתנא דמחייב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:2:1.english: According to Rabba, [it is] certainly - Perforce he establishes his statement as [a dispute between] tanna'im, for he said [that the assailant is] liable, and that [baraita] which teaches [that he is] exempt he cannot establish in accordance with his [view]; and perforce he answers thus: "I state [my ruling] in accordance with the tanna who holds [him] liable."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:2:2.hebrew: אלא לרב חסדא מי לימא - מי מיבעיא ליה לאוקמיה מילתא בפלוגתא כתנאי, ולמימר "אנא דאמרי כתנא דפטר", או מצי לתרוצי האי דתנא "חייב" במילתא אחריתי, דלא תקשי ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:2:2.english: But according to Rav Ḥisda, shall we say - Does he need to establish the matter as a dispute of tanna’im, and say, "I state [my opinion] in accordance with the tanna who exempts," or can he resolve the [baraita] that taught "liable" [as referring] to another matter, so that it will not be difficult for him?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:3:1.hebrew: לא קשיא - כלומר, אמר לך רב חסדא: תרוייהו תנאי כוותי קיימי, דבדמי ולדות פטור, והא דתניא חייב — בשבת ולדות, ואליבא דר"ש דאמר אשה פלגא בהו, והיא קיימת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:3:1.english: It is not difficult - That is to say, Rav Ḥisda [could] say to you: Both Tannaim stand in accordance with my [view], for regarding the value of the offspring he is exempt, and that which was taught [in the baraita] that he is liable [refers] to the increase in [the woman's] value due to the offspring, and [this is] in accordance with R. Shimon [ben Gamliel], who says [that] the woman [has] a half [share] in it, and she is alive.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:3:2.hebrew: והא - דתני פטור, רבנן היא, דאמרי כולהו דבעל, והרי הוא מת וזכה זה מן ההפקר. אבל רבה לא מצי לתרוצי מידי, דהא איהו אמר: אשה זכתה בחלק בעלה מן ההפקר, הואיל והיא היתה מעוברת ומוחזקת בהן בשעת מיתה, ואמאי פטור משבח ולדות? ודמי ולדות דידה נינהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:3:2.english: And this - [baraita] that teaches [that he is] exempt is [in accordance with] the Rabbis, who say [that] all of it belongs to the husband; and behold, he has died, so this [assailant] acquired [it] from ownerless property. However, Rabbah cannot resolve [the contradiction] at all, for he said [that] the woman acquired her husband's share from ownerless property, since she was pregnant and in possession of them at the time of [his] death — so why would he be exempt from [paying for] the increase in value due to the offspring? And the value of the offspring is [also] hers.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:4:1.hebrew: מאי אריא לאחר מיתת - הגר, דתני חייב ליתן לה חלקה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:4:1.english: Why specifically after the death of - the convert, where it teaches, "he is obligated to give her her share."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:4:3.english: Also - [He is] obligated to give her her share.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:4:5.english: All of it - For she acquires her husband's share of the appreciation of the offspring.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:6:1.hebrew: אמרי - א"כ, קשיא לרב חסדא: דמשבח ולדות — המגיע חציו בחיי הגר לגר, וקאמר ר"ש דכשמת והיא מעוברת זכתה היא בחלקו — נשמע דזכתה נמי בדמי ולדות דבעלה, דמאי שנא דמי ולדות משבח ולדות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:6:1.english: They said - If so, it is difficult for Rav Chisda: for from [the law of] the increase [in value] due to the offspring — half of which goes to the convert during the convert's lifetime, and Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel] says that when he dies while she is pregnant, she acquires his portion — let us derive that she also acquires the compensation for [miscarried] offspring belonging to her husband, for what is the difference between compensation for offspring and the increase [in value] due to offspring?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:6:2.hebrew: ומדר"ש - דאשמעינן דזכתה בחלקו, נשמע נמי לרבנן דזכתה בכולן, דרבנן לא פליגי אלא במחיים, אבל בזכיה דמיתה לא פליגי רבנן ור"ש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:6:2.english: And from [that of] Rabbi Shimon - Since he taught us that she acquired his share, let us also derive for the Rabbis that she acquired all of them, for the Rabbis only disagree during [the husband's] lifetime, but regarding acquisition upon death, the Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon do not disagree.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:7:1.english: They said - Compensation for [miscarried] offspring is not comparable to the increase [in value due to] offspring.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:7:2.hebrew: שבח ולדות - לר"ש, דשייכא בהו מחיים בפלגא, כי מיית זכייא בכולהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:7:2.english: Increase [due to] the offspring - According to Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel], since she has a share in them during [her husband's] lifetime for half, when he dies she acquires all of them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:8:1.english: Of the documents of a convert - [Documents] in which another Jew mortgaged his lands to him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:8:2.english: What is [the law] - To acquire the paper.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:8:3.hebrew: ושטרא נמי לא קני - ואי אתא ישראל אחר והחזיק בה לצור על פי צלוחיתו, קנייה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:8:3.english: And he does not acquire the document either - And if another Jew comes and takes possession of it to tie [it] over the mouth of his flask, he acquires it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:9:1.english: Answer, my Master - Answer me, my lord.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 49b:9:2.english: And [does he need it] to cover the mouth of his flask - [i.e.,] that his intention should be on the document from the outset (and his intention is not on the land)?

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:10:1.hebrew: משכונו של ישראל ביד גר כו' מוציאין אותו מידו - ואפילו משכנו שלא בשעת הלואתו, ואפילו למ"ד בעל חוב קונה משכון, דע"כ אין לו אלא שעבוד עליו, כיון שהיה יכול לפדותו הישראל ולסלקו בדמים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:10:1.english: "The collateral of a Jew in the possession of a convert, etc., [the court] appropriates it from his possession" - And [this applies] even if he took it as collateral not at the time of his loan, and even according to the one who says [that] a creditor acquires the collateral, for perforce he has only a lien upon it, since the Jew was able to redeem it and pay him off with money.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:14:1.hebrew: והלכתא דליתיה בחצר - פ"ה דאמשכון קאי, דאם איתיה בחצר קני, אע"פ שאין עומד בצד שדהו. וצריך לומר דאיירי בחצר המשתמרת, דאי בחצר שאין משתמרת, לא קנה אלא אם כן עומד בצד שדהו, כדאיתא בפ"ק דב"מ (דף יא. ושם.). ולמאי דס"ד דאיירי כשהמשכון בחצר ובעל החצר אין כאן — זה אינו כפי המסקנא של ב"מ. ולר"י נראה דמעיקרא נמי הכי ס"ל, דאיירי בחצר שאין משתמרת, ולא קנה אלא אם כן עומד בצד שדהו; וכן משמע נמי מ"בא זה והחזיק בה": אם כן, לא היתה משתמרת אצל זה. והא דקאמר "והלכתא דליתיה בחצר" — אבעל חצר קאי, כלומר: שינויא דשנינן שינויא הוא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:14:1.english: And the halakha is that where he/it is not in the courtyard - Rashi explained that [this] refers to the collateral: that if it is in the courtyard, he acquires [it], even though he is not standing beside his field. And one must say that it is dealing with a guarded courtyard, for if [it were] an unguarded courtyard, he does not acquire [it] unless he is standing beside his field, as is stated in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (11a, and there). And according to what one might have thought, that it deals with [a case] where the collateral is in the courtyard and the owner of the courtyard is not here — this is not in accordance with the conclusion of Bava Metzia. And it appears to the Ri that from the outset as well, [the Gemara] held thus: that it deals with an unguarded courtyard, and he does not acquire [it] unless he is standing beside his field; and so is also implied from "this one came and took possession of it": if so, it was not guarded by this [creditor]. And that which [the Gemara] says, "And the halakha is that where he is not in the courtyard," refers to the owner of the courtyard; that is to say, the answer that we answered is [indeed] an answer.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:15:1.hebrew: החופר בור ברה"י ופתחו לרה"ר - כללא דמילתא בכל הך שמעתתא: בור בתר פתחו אזלינן, דנחשב הבור כאילו הוא במקום שהפתח שם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:15:1.english: One who digs a pit on private property and its opening [is] to the public domain - The general principle of the matter throughout this entire discussion [is that with regard to] a pit, we follow its opening, for the pit is considered as if it is in the place where the opening is.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:15:2.hebrew: ברה"י ופתחו לרה"י אחר - פ"ה שהפקיר רשותו, אותה שפי הבור בתוכה. אין נראה שר"ל שפתחו לרה"י של אדם אחר ובא אותו אדם והפקיר רשותו, שלא היה לו לומר "אותה" בלשון נקבה, אלא משמע שרוצה לפרש הכל ברשות עצמו. ולשון "אחר" אינו מיושב לפירוש זה. ואין להקשות אמאי אצטריך למתני "ברה"י ופתחו לרה"י אחר", ה"ל למימר "החופר בור ברה"י" ותו לא — דאגב אחריני נקט הכי, ופירש לנו שהבור והפתח הכל עושה ברשותו. ור"י מפרש: "ברה"י ופתחו לרה"י אחר" — דהיינו שחפר בור ברשות עצמו ופתחו לרשות חבירו. ואצטריך, דלא תימא פתחו לרה"ר הוא דחייב דשכיחי רבים ומזקי, אבל ברה"י דליכא למיחש אלא לנזק יחידי — פטור. וכה"ג תניא בהמניח (לעיל בבא קמא לב:) גבי המבקע. ולפי פי' ר"י קשה: למה הוא חייב בנזקי בעל חצר אם נפל שורו לבור? כיון שהחופר משלם נזקי החצר, על בעל חצר למלוייה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:15:2.english: In private property and opens it into another private property - Rashi explained that he declared his property ownerless — the one in which the mouth of the pit is located. It does not appear that he means to say that he opened it into another person's private property and that person came and declared his property ownerless, for [if so] he should not have said "otah" ["it"] in the feminine; rather, it implies that he means to explain [that] everything [is] in his own property. And the wording "another" is not well-settled according to this explanation. And one should not object: Why was it necessary to teach "in private property and opens it into another private property"? It should have said "One who digs a pit in private property" and nothing more! — For on account of the other [cases] it phrased it thus, and it explained to us that the pit and the opening — he makes everything in his own property. And Ri explains: "In private property and opens it into another private property" — that is, he dug a pit in his own property and opened it into his fellow's property. And it was necessary [to state this], so that you should not say: It is only when he opens it into the public domain that he is liable, because many people are common there and it causes damage, whereas in private property, where there is only concern for the damage of an individual, he is exempt. And similarly it is taught in [the chapter] HaMeniach (above, Bava Kamma 32b) regarding one who chops [wood]. And according to Ri's explanation, it is difficult: Why is he liable for the damages of the owner of the courtyard if his ox fell into the pit? Since the digger pays for the damages to the courtyard, it is upon the owner of the courtyard to fill it in.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:15:3.hebrew: ברה"ר ופתחו לרה"י - פירש בקונט': והפקיר רשותו. וה"ה אם מתחילה סמכיה לרה"ר, ולא הוצרך לפרש בהפקיר רשותו אלא משום דמשמע ליה לישנא ד"פתחו לרה"י" באמצע רה"י, כדמוכח בגמרא דקתני "ברה"ר ופתחו לרה"י פטור", דמוקי שלא הפקיר לא רשותו ולא בורו, ומעיקרא ס"ד כשהפקיר רשותו ולא בורו; והיינו משום דמשמע ליה "ופתחו לרה"י" באמצע רה"י:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:15:3.english: "[In] the public domain and opened it into a private domain" - Rashi explained: [this is where] he renounced ownership of his property. And the same applies if from the outset he placed it adjacent to the public domain, and [Rashi] only needed to explain [it] as [a case where] he renounced ownership of his property because the phrasing "opened it into a private domain" implies to him [that the opening is] in the middle of the private domain — as is proven in the Gemara, which teaches: "[If he dug] in the public domain and opened it into a private domain, he is exempt," which [the Gemara] establishes [as referring to a case] where he renounced ownership of neither his property nor his pit, whereas initially it had assumed [it refers to a case] where he renounced ownership of his property but not his pit; and that is because "and opened it into a private domain" implies to it [that the opening is] in the middle of the private domain.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:16:1.hebrew: ת"ר החופר בור ברה"י ופתחו לרה"ר - וי"ס שכתוב בהן ברה"ר ופתחו לרה"ר, והכי מתניא בתוספתא (פ"ו). וק"ק דה"ל למימר "החופר בור ברה"ר", אבל אין להקפיד, משום דקאי אהנך דמתניתין דאיירי שהפתח ברשות אחרת, אצטריך לאשמועינן דאיירי באותו ענין שהבור והפתח במקום אחד ברשות הרבים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:16:1.english: The Sages taught: One who digs a pit in a private domain and opens it to the public domain - And there are texts in which it is written "in the public domain and opens it to the public domain," and so it is taught in the Tosefta (ch. 6). And it is somewhat difficult, for it should have said [simply] "One who digs a pit in the public domain"; however, one need not be particular [about this], because since [the baraita] refers to those [cases] of the Mishnah that deal [with a case] where the opening is in another domain, it needed to teach us that [this clause] is dealing with a case where the pit and the opening are in one place, in the public domain.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:17:1.hebrew: על הכרייה לא כ"ש - במכלתין אמרינן: "מכאן שאין עונשין מן הדין", אבל בש"ס שלנו אין סובר כן, כדפרישית בריש המסכת (דף ב.). [עיין תוס' לעיל (בבא קמא ד':) ד"ה ועדים]:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:17:1.english: "For digging, is it not all the more so?!" - In the Mekhilta we say: "From here [we derive] that we do not punish based on an a fortiori derivation." However, in our Talmud it does not hold so, as I explained at the beginning of the tractate (2a). [See Tosafot above (Bava Kamma 4b), s.v. Ve'edim.]

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:1:1.hebrew: ותני זכתה - ואין מגיה הברייתא, אלא כלומר: "זכה" — מי שיש לו זכות:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 49b:1:1.english: And teach: "She acquires" [zakhtah] - And [the Gemara] is not emending the baraita; rather, it means to say: "He acquires" [refers to] whoever has the right [to the compensation].
